host.docker.bar: Docker and the compose plugin are installed
fix: Install Docker Engine and the compose plugin: https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/
Run `lpo up` again.

host.disk.bar: at least 20 GiB free where Docker stores images
host.disk.why: images and rendered outputs need space
fix: Free disk space or grow the volume.
Run `lpo up` again.

node.config.bar: lpo.yaml is complete and the Kit files are rendered
node.config.why: the node and runners are configured from lpo.yaml
fix: Fill in the fields named in Measured.
Run `lpo up` again.

node.running.bar: the orchestrator, Caddy and runner containers are running
node.running.why: nothing can serve until the stack is up
fix: Read the logs: `docker compose logs --tail 50 <service>`.
Run `lpo up` again.

net.public_ip.bar: the host name resolves to a public address
net.public_ip.why: the network reaches you by this name
fix: Point an A record for your host at this machine's public IP.

net.tls.why: the network only talks to you over TLS
fix: Open ports 80 and 443 so Caddy can get a certificate.
Check `docker compose logs caddy`.

chain.keystore.bar: the wallet keystore, password and RPC URL files exist and the keystore address equals eth_address
chain.keystore.why: the node signs and receives payments with this key
fix: New wallet: run `lpo wallet`; it asks for a password and an Arbitrum One RPC URL and keeps everything in secrets/.
Existing wallet: put its keystore at secrets/wallet-keystore, its password at secrets/wallet-password and an Arbitrum One RPC URL at secrets/arbitrum-rpc-url (all mode 600).
Never paste the key or password into chat or a ticket.

chain.active.bar: eth_address is in the active orchestrator set this round
chain.active.why: paid work only goes to active orchestrators
fix: Fund the address on Arbitrum One with about 0.01 ETH and enough LPT; `lpo register --lpt <amount>` shows the stake needed.
Run `lpo register --lpt <amount>` (dry run), then again with --submit: it bonds, registers and sets your service URI.
Wait for the next round (about a day), then run `lpo up` again.

chain.service_uri.bar: the on-chain service URI is https://<host>, or you know why it is not
chain.service_uri.why: chain-based discovery finds you at the on-chain URI; a different URI is fine for a second host but changing it moves all on-chain traffic
fix: If this machine should be your main host, set the service URI to https://<host> on Arbitrum One.
If another host already serves this address, leave the URI alone; this host is reached through the network's orchestrator list.

runner.listed.why: the network only sends jobs to apps your node lists
fix: Check the runner logs: `docker compose logs --tail 50 hyperframes`.
Run `lpo up` again.

runner.host.bar: every runner URL in /discovery is on your host
runner.host.why: selection refuses runners on another host
fix: Keep runners behind the Kit's Caddy; do not list other hosts.

manifest.match.bar: lpo.yaml and /discovery agree on app, mode and price
manifest.match.why: a mismatch means the published price is not what you charge
fix: Run `lpo up` to re-render and restart.

price.ceiling.bar: each price is at or below the network ceiling
price.ceiling.why: the signer refuses prices above its ceiling
fix: Lower price_info.price in lpo.yaml, then run `lpo up`.

cap.contract.bar: a sample request returns the declared output (an MP4 with frames)
cap.contract.why: the network tests the same contract before paying you
fix: Read the evidence below and the runner logs, fix the runner, then run `lpo up` again.
